title: Some of you are insufferable
author: GosenSidewinder
selftext:
Not every game needs to be original or better than an existing game.

I started following this sub a few weeks ago just to see the games other people are making. It seems like almost every time someone shares their game, some a-hole asks "how is it better" or "how is it unique" compared to some hugely popular or genre defining game.

Nobody wants to see exact clones, but can you guys stop with the implied negativity just because someone wants to make a game that isn't completely original?

Most games aren't original, and most aren't even "better" than the games that came before them. Entire genres of near-clones already existed before AI (mobas, extraction shooters, etc etc etc).

Not every game needs to reinvent the wheel. Sometimes people just want to make their own version of something they enjoy.

comments.author: Initial_Plastic_8069
comments.body: You are posting here for feedback, right ? What else do you expect

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: Then give feedback. "How is it better" is pretty weak feedback and (not always) but often comes off negatively the way it's said

replies.author: Initial_Plastic_8069
replies.body: things are not such like Alice in Wonderland .

comments.author: MrMegaPhoenix
comments.body:
If you are a major game publisher and you make a blatant ripoff of overwatch, Fortnite, call of duty, gta, etc, you will get people noticing and calm it unoriginal 

If you are an ai game developer having ai make your game and you make a blatant ripoff, what do you think will happen?

At the very least, you should be clear you know it’s a ripoff when posting

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: I'm not talking about blatant rip offs, I thought I was clear about that

replies.author: MrMegaPhoenix
replies.body:
If they want to make their own version of “game”, that sounds like a ripoff 

If they aren’t, then yeah they shouldn’t be judged 

But most are clearly ripoffs and then people get defensive about it and it looks silly.

comments.author: PoopsMcScoots
comments.body:
I definitely think the mods need to push for professional attitude.

That means both stomping out the name-calling and unprofessionalism.

But also getting a thicker skin and stop expecting to only get praise for everything.

comments.author: Carter5on
comments.body: Generally, there is no parthenogenesis. Don't stress over that. Everyone is drawing inspiration from everyone and everything. Take their feedback (which is free by the way), use it as you please and keep moving forward.

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: Agreed, just seeing negativity for no reason, felt like yelling at clouds

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body:
\>Edit: I'm just suggesting some of you judge games here on their own merit and by the effort put into them

I think that's exactly what we're doing when we criticize something that very closely clones another game's identity.

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: I feel like I see it in all posts though, not just the games that are straight up clones.

comments.author: 0DayMaker
comments.body: Stop making blatant knockoffs of existing games? No one is mad about something that resembles a game, but has its own identity. Much of what's being posted is literally just on the level of "I made X with AI", and it's not even the full game, it's just some shitty tech demo.

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: I agree with you but my point is exactly that it seems to be happening in all or most threads, including where people are making a genuine effort

comments.author: hauntolog
comments.body:
We ARE judging them on their own merit. What's their use if they are lesser copies of something that already exists? For a more conventional example, why did the new God of War Metroidvania flop? That's a money printing IP. But there are loads of amazing games that do what it tries to do far better. So it's not worth people's time, money or attention. At least people got paid to make that game. When you make lesser, uncreative clones of games, you are not generating any value for anyone, you are just taking up resources and pumping out things that "only a mother could love", in the sense of, it's special to you because you were involved in making it, but it's of zero worth to anyone else.

Why are halfbaked, mediocre at best, projects worth our time an attention? Why should we bother with lesser copies, mindlessly churned out just because they can?

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body:
> What's their use if they are lesser copies of something that already exists?

You are describing most games even before AI. You're kind of making my point for me.

replies.author: hauntolog
replies.body: Do you think if these AI projects were similar to the games you speak of they wouldn't have the same reception by people? I think they are by and large more lacking, in completion, in polish, in cohesion, among other things. Nobody is speaking about God of War Sons of Sparta, even though it had the entire Sony marketing machine and a beloved IP behind it.

comments.author: RarScary
comments.body:
Here's the problem:  Until the dev adds a unique story, twist, or mechanic that sets it apart, it remains a clone of something already done and probably done better.  It's fair criticism.  But people aren't also presenting things as prototypes or early demos, they're presenting things as games.  So again, open to fair criticism.

But the main reason everyone is sensitive to people posting clones and copies is this whole sub is struggling with a negative bias and collectively pushes against anyone posting something that would reinforce that sentiment.  It's understandable that people are critical and want to push people beyond their copycats.

TLDR: The community wants to be divorced of the AI slop label, but there's a shit ton of AI slop posted here.

replies.author: GosenSidewinder
replies.body: Well thought out reply. My point is that, at least in most of the threads I've read (I don't see them all) - there are people being overly negative without any actual feedback on games that are genuine efforts, just because they are not 100% original

replies.author: RarScary
replies.body:
and I agree with you there.  Nobody is making truly "unique" games and a lot of people posting are just excited about their project and getting torn to shreds.

It's a wakeup call I think a lot of people in this sub need, but a little tact wouldn't hurt.  And blanket statements simply calling something unoriginal aren't terribly helpful and just make the sub toxic.

comments.author: Opulon_Nelva
comments.body:
Yesterday, for my 5 dollars of daily attention, I had the choice between 10 burgers. I looked at them each 10 seconds, and made a choice.

Today, for my 5 dollars, I have the choice between 100 burgers. 

Each has one second, and I'm growing tired by the 50th nearly identical I'm looking at.

I begin to pick subtle clues and patterns, to know how I can ignore most of them in half a second instead of a single. My brain begins to focus on identifying what makes a burger different from the very narrow median. 

The burger makers are whining that I do not give a fair chance to their burgers. I understand their philosophy, but I see that tomorrow 200 burger makers have registered for my 5 dollars of attention.


Ceiling is raising, standards are following quickly. 

 Customer decides in this regard, whether you like it or not, and on this sub you have amongst the most lenient potential customers.

comments.author: WiredBrew
comments.body:
Nah. I just think there's two camps of people who use AI. 

People who spent a long time learning how to make games that are now using AI to accelerate their own development and make things they realistically couldn't make before due to time/budget constraints. 

And people who have zero understanding of the game dev process and are telling Claude to one shot an existing game and/or posting shit like "pixel art" with 30 shades per ramp and mismatched pixel density between every sprite. 

It's a natural form of community self-policing because people don't want AI game dev to forever associated with with stealing other people's games and churning out absolute slow.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
>Not every game needs to be original or better than an existing game.

AI has *raised* the bar for expected quality, not lowered it. Being original or better is the expectation now.

>some a-hole asks "how is it better" or "how is it unique" compared to some hugely popular or genre defining game.

Those are entirely valid questions to be asked when you're asking for feedback on a game you're making. Most devs ask those questions *themselves* while they're developing. If it's not better and not unique, it doesn't stand out. That means it's going to get buried into obscurity, especially if it's just a cheap knock-off of an existing game.

If someone's making something like that for personal use, that's fine. Many folks around here are not doing that. They're trying to make a quick buck by releasing slop, which gives all the folks here who are putting time and effort into things a bad rep.
